correctness.rationale: For the one-edge graph E, U(x)=E(x,x) selects originals, and deterministic sink-chain tests C_i(t),T_i(z) are forward-local: successor closure preserves their exact truth. An edge-node path a->z->b with T_i(z) interprets R_i(a,b); any E-successor-closed induced graph H produces precisely the induced interpreted source structure on U(H), with all R_i-successors of any retained a also retained. Every finite all-binary source A has an explicit realization F(A) using original looped vertices, one edge node per source tuple and an i-long sink chain, and I(F(A))=A exactly, including loops and empty. The critical reflection induction partitions vertices into finitely many sorts (original, edge, tag), translates E/equality literals by parameter equalities and R_i-literals, universal quantifiers by finite conjunctions of unrestricted universals, and E-guarded quantifiers by the exact finite outgoing-list; original-to-edge successors require only R_i-guarded source quantifiers, while edge/tag successors are deterministic, so no unguarded existential is introduced. Therefore any hypothetical E-language ∃-bounded equivalent would pull back to a multi-relation ∃-bounded equivalent, contradicting the explicitly verified van Benthem–ten Cate–Yang Theorem 8 and Lemmas 9–10. Source check_generated_coding.py was read including finite sample limits; finite tests alone not proof. Source χ is universal and true on empty structures, so the interpretation covers empty cases.
